candidate_relations.reason: Discoid lupus would not show atypical CD4 lymphocytes entering follicular epithelium with a CD4:CD8 ratio >7:1 and monoclonal TCR.
Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides fits the follicular CD4 clone and mucin but omits that disease is confined to one eyelid plaque.
Pagetoid reticulosis is an epidermotropic unilesional CTCL, whereas this infiltrate is perifollicular with infundibular tropism and only mild mucin.
Granuloma faciale is a chronic facial vasculitis/eosinophilic infiltrate, not a CD4-restricted clonal folliculotropic lymphoma.
Follicular mucinosis is present only focally and, with monoclonal T cells, is a component of folliculotropic MF rather than idiopathic FM.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is the parent neoplasm and omits folliculotropism and the solitary plaque.
Jessner lymphocytic infiltrate is a benign CD8-leaning dermal T-cell infiltrate without atypical follicular exocytosis or clonality.
Lymphoma is a remote parent and does not specify unilesional folliculotropic mycosis fungoides.
Unilesional folliculotropic mycosis fungoides matches the single 4 × 2 cm eyelid plaque with clonal folliculotropic CD4 cells.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma names the lineage but not the folliculotropic unilesional phenotype.
Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia is a reactive process contradicted by atypical intraepithelial lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell rearrangement.
Cutaneous lymphoma is still a parent category missing both folliculotropism and unilesional distribution.
